content: Phenobarbital affects the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4, CYP2B6, and CYP2C19, leading to significant drug interactions. Below are the detailed interactions: 1. Tramadol and O-desmethyltramadol: Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 inducers, such as phenobarbital, reduces the area under the curve (AUC) of tramadol and its active metabolite, decreasing their therapeutic effects. Monitor closely. 2. Trazodone: Phenobarbital decreases trazodone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation, necessitating caution and monitoring. 3. Triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension: Phenobarbital reduces its levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 4. Triazolam: Phenobarbital decreases triazolam levels via CYP3A4 induction. Both drugs increase sedation, requiring careful monitoring. 5. Triclabendazole: This drug increases phenobarbital levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitor plasma concentrations of CYP2C19 substrates during and after triclabendazole therapy. 6. Triclofos: Both phenobarbital and triclofos enhance sedation. Use with caution and monitor. 7. Trifluoperazine: Both drugs increase sedation. Monitor for additive effects. 8. Belladonna alkaloids and trihexyphenidyl: Both reduce cholinergic effects, potentially leading to additive anticholinergic effects. Monitor closely. 9. Trimipramine: Phenobarbital reduces trimipramine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Both drugs increase sedation. Monitor for reduced efficacy and additive sedation. 10. Triprolidine: Both drugs increase sedation. Use with caution and monitor. 11. Trospium chloride and belladonna alkaloids: Both reduce cholinergic transmission, leading to additive anticholinergic effects. Monitor closely. 12. Trofinetide: Increases phenobarbital levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates for potential toxicities. 13. Umeclidinium bromide and belladonna alkaloids: Both reduce cholinergic effects. Avoid co-administration of additional anticholinergic agents if possible. 14. Ustekinumab: Chronic inflammation may alter CYP450 enzyme formation. Monitor therapeutic effects of CYP450 substrates when initiating or discontinuing ustekinumab. 15. Vardenafil: Phenobarbital reduces vardenafil levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 16. Vecuronium and belladonna alkaloids: Both reduce cholinergic transmission. Monitor for additive effects. 17. Verapamil: Phenobarbital decreases verapamil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 18. Vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled: Phenobarbital reduces their levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects. 19. Vilazodone: Phenobarbital decreases vilazodone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Consider increasing the vilazodone dose up to twofold (not exceeding 80 mg/day) when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers for more than 14 days. 20. Viloxazine: Increases phenobarbital levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates and adjust doses as needed. 21. Vinblastine, vincristine, and vincristine liposomal: Phenobarbital reduces their levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 22. Vitamin D: Phenobarbital reduces vitamin D levels, potentially requiring supplementation or dosage adjustments in patients on chronic anticonvulsant therapy. 23. Vortioxetine: Phenobarbital increases vortioxetine metabolism, reducing its levels. Consider increasing the vortioxetine dose (up to threefold) when co-administered with strong CYP inducers for more than 14 days. 24. Warfarin: Phenobarbital reduces warfarin levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitor INR and adjust warfarin dose as needed. 25. Xylometazoline and yohimbine: Phenobarbital increases sedation, while these agents decrease it. The interaction effect is unclear; use with caution. 26. Ziconotide: Both phenobarbital and ziconotide increase sedation. Monitor for additive effects. 27. Ziprasidone: Belladonna alkaloids reduce ziprasidone levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Phenobarbital also increases sedation when combined with ziprasidone. Monitor for additive effects. 28. Zotepine: Belladonna alkaloids reduce zotepine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Phenobarbital increases sedation when combined with zotepine. Monitor for additive effects. 29. Acetaminophen (oral, IV, rectal): Phenobarbital increases acetaminophen metabolism, potentially enhancing hepatotoxic metabolite levels. Monitor for hepatotoxicity. 30. Acetazolamide: Co-administration with phenobarbital increases the risk of anticonvulsant-induced osteomalacia. Monitor bone health. 31. Alfentanil: Phenobarbital reduces alfentanil levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 32. Alfuzosin: Phenobarbital decreases alfuzosin levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 33. Alosetron: Phenobarbital reduces alosetron levels via CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 34. Alvimopan: Phenobarbital reduces alvimopan levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 35. Ambrisentan: Phenobarbital reduces ambrisentan levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 36. Amitriptyline: Phenobarbital increases metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), reducing their blood concentrations. Toxic doses of TCAs may lead to respiratory depression. Monitor closely. 37. Amoxapine: Similar to amitriptyline, phenobarbital increases metabolism of TCAs, reducing their efficacy. Monitor closely. 38. Amphotericin B deoxycholate: Phenobarbital reduces its levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 39. Antipyrine: Phenobarbital reduces antipyrine levels via CYP1A2 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 40. Armodafinil: Phenobarbital reduces armodafinil levels via CYP3A4 induction and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 41. Ascorbic acid: Phenobarbital increases ascorbic acid elimination, reducing its levels. Monitor for deficiency. 42. Asenapine: Phenobarbital reduces asenapine levels via CYP1A2 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 43. Ashwagandha: Enhances phenobarbital’s CNS depressant effects via pharmacodynamic synergism. Monitor for increased sedation. 44. Atracurium: Phenobarbital reduces atracurium’s effects via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 45. Biotin: Phenobarbital reduces biotin levels through an unspecified mechanism. Biotin supplementation may be necessary. 46. Bosentan: Phenobarbital reduces bosentan levels via CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 47. Brimonidine: Enhances phenobarbital’s CNS depressant effects via pharmacodynamic synergism. Monitor for increased sedation. 48. Brinzolamide: Co-administration with phenobarbital increases the risk of anticonvulsant-induced osteomalacia. Monitor bone health. 49. Caffeine: Phenobarbital reduces caffeine levels via CYP1A2 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 50. Celecoxib: Phenobarbital reduces celecoxib levels via CYP2C9/10 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 51. Cevimeline: Phenobarbital reduces cevimeline levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 52. Chloramphenicol: Phenobarbital increases chloramphenicol metabolism, reducing its levels. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 53. Chlorpromazine: Phenobarbital increases chlorpromazine metabolism, reducing its levels. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 54. Cimetidine: Phenobarbital reduces cimetidine levels via CYP2C19 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 55. Cisatracurium: Phenobarbital reduces cisatracurium’s effects via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 56. Clarithromycin: Phenobarbital reduces clarithromycin levels by increasing elimination. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 57. Clomipramine: Phenobarbital increases metabolism of TCAs, reducing their blood concentrations. Toxic doses of TCAs may lead to respiratory depression. Monitor closely. 58. Clotrimazole: Phenobarbital reduces clotrimazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 59. Cocaine topical: Phenobarbital reduces cocaine levels via CYP2B6 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 60. Cyanocobalamin: Phenobarbital reduces cyanocobalamin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Monitor for deficiency. 61. Dapsone: Phenobarbital reduces dapsone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 62. Desipramine: Phenobarbital increases metabolism of TCAs, reducing their blood concentrations. Toxic doses of TCAs may lead to respiratory depression. Monitor closely. 63. Dexmethylphenidate: Reduces phenobarbital metabolism, increasing its effects. Monitor for enhanced sedation. 64. Dimenhydrinate: Increases belladonna alkaloid toxicity via pharmacodynamic synergism. Monitor for additive anticholinergic effects. 65. Diazepam: Phenobarbital reduces diazepam levels via CYP2C19 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 66. Diclofenac: Phenobarbital reduces diclofenac levels via CYP2C9/10 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 67. Disopyramide: Phenobarbital reduces disopyramide levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 68. Docetaxel: Phenobarbital reduces docetaxel levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 69. Donepezil: Phenobarbital reduces donepezil levels via CYP3A4 induction. Donepezil also antagonizes belladonna alkaloid effects. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 70. Dosulepin: Phenobarbital increases metabolism of TCAs, reducing their blood concentrations. Toxic doses of TCAs may lead to respiratory depression. Monitor closely. 71. Galantamine: Antagonizes belladonna alkaloid effects. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 72. Doxepin: Phenobarbital increases metabolism of TCAs, reducing their blood concentrations. Toxic doses of TCAs may lead to respiratory depression. Monitor closely. 73. Dutasteride: Phenobarbital reduces dutasteride levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 74. Efavirenz: Phenobarbital reduces efavirenz levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 75. Eplerenone: Phenobarbital reduces eplerenone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 76. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate): Phenobarbital increases erythromycin elimination, reducing its levels. Monitor for reduced efficacy.
